_comment: Mutation testing: it grades the TESTS, not the code.
Stryker changes the source — flips > to >=, alters constants, deletes lines —
and reports which changes the suite fails to notice. A surviving mutant is a
line no test actually constrains. This automates the discipline the repo
already states: verified by mutation, not by going green. Two tests written
this week passed for the wrong reason and were caught by hand; this finds that
SCOPE IS DELIBERATE. Every mutant re-runs the suite, so the DB-backed suites
against real Postgres would make a full run punishing and mostly uninformative
— those tests are about wiring, and a mutant there usually fails loudly.
What is in scope is the arithmetic that decides who gets paid, plus the pure
policy modules. Per CLAUDE.md, a wrong constant here 'is not a crash, it is a
silently wrong royalty found on mainnet' — precisely where a test that cannot
npm run mutate            everything in scope
npm run mutate -- --mutate src/tx-result.ts    one file, fast
_thresholds_comment: high/low are advisory colour bands. `break` is the one that matters: below it
the run exits non-zero. Set just under the current score (79.42) so it is a
ratchet — a regression fails, and the number rises as survivors get killed.
Never lower it to make a run pass; that is the one move that makes this
_tsconfig_comment: Points at a file that does not exist ON PURPOSE, and this is a workaround.
Stryker's TSConfigPreprocessor rewrites tsconfig paths for the sandbox by
calling ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson, which TypeScript 7 REMOVED. Every
Stryker version through 9.6.1 still calls it, so any run dies with
'ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson is not a function' the moment it finds a
tsconfig. Naming one that is absent skips the preprocessor entirely, which is
harmless here: the sandbox runs vitest through its own esbuild transform and
never consults tsconfig. Delete this the day Stryker supports TS 7.
_scope_comment: src/ledger.ts is the most valuable target and is deliberately NOT here yet.
All the money math lives in it — platformFeeDrops, spendableFrom, bidHeadroom,
auctionSellAmountDrops — but so do 11 network call sites, so its mutants pull
in the DB-backed suites. Stryker runs those concurrently against the same
Postgres, which is the fixture collision already measured at ~20% failures
when anything else touches that database. A separate test database is the
prerequisite; add ledger.ts the day that exists.
